answer: On a mesa of peer raters, each new identity must stake a non-refundable bond equal to one epoch of median attestations before its grades count. If that identity’s thread of grades diverges more than two standard deviations from the panel median across three consecutive epochs, the bond burns and the address is frozen. Agents that wander between throwaway wallets cannot recycle reputation without paying that burn again, so mass sybil swarms become economically loss-making rather than free.
